newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian government approves two power projects.
newsitem.headline: Indian government approves two power projects.

text.p: India's Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) has approved a proposal for setting up Stage I of a 400 megawatt capacity gas power project in the northern state of Haryana, a government spokesman said on Tuesday.
The project, to be part financed by Japan's Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund, is expected to cost 11.63 billion rupees ($325 million).
It will be set up in Faridabad, near the Indian capital and executed by the state-run National Thermal Power Corporation, the spokesman said. The power will be allocated to Haryana.
The CCEA also approved a proposal for setting up two 500 MW plants for the Simhedra Thermal Power project, in southern Andhra Pradesh state.
The project, to be executed by NTPC, is expected to cost 36.50 billion rupees.
